Join us to build Duolingo Ads, Duolingo’s premium programmatic business. Most learners use our free, ad‑supported app—so great ads are core to our mission. Reporting into the Head of Ad Sales, the Ad Sales Lead, Programmatic will build a deal‑led book of business with agency holding companies, independent agencies, and advertisers who want access to Duolingo’s native formats, first‑party learner signals, and one of the most engaged mobile audiences in the world. You will own buy‑side relationships across holdco investment and programmatic teams, trading desks, curation and principal media groups, and premium programmatic buyers. This is a high‑ownership, high‑visibility, early‑stage opportunity to help define how programmatic can fuel high‑quality ads for millions of learners while driving outcomes for partners.

🧠 You will...

• Own a programmatic revenue target and forecast, and build a predictable pipeline across agency holding‑company programmatic and investment teams, trading desks, independent agencies, and premium programmatic buyers.

• Lead our shift from open auction to premium, deal‑led PMP/PG by packaging Duolingo’s native formats and first‑party learner signals into always‑on and custom deals that buyers will pay a premium for, and negotiate annual and upfront commitments that make that revenue durable.

• Become the person holdco programmatic teams call about mobile app inventory: run joint business planning; get Duolingo onto preferred supply paths, curated marketplaces, and principal/outcome‑based buys; and defend our position when buyers consolidate

• Build the programmatic value proposition and measurement story through proposals, pricing narratives, and post‑campaign proof that connect our native formats and audience data to brand and performance outcomes (e.g., verification, attention, brand lift, incrementality, MMM).

• Partner with Ad Platform Operations and Ad Ops on deal setup, targeting, floors, pacing, and troubleshooting—ensuring what you sell is deliverable and delivers against expectations.

• Work alongside our direct sellers under clear rules of engagement so programmatic expands the account through incremental value; coordinate with Account Management pre‑ and post‑sale to drive renewal and expansion.

• Feed structured market intelligence back to sales, product, and engineering leadership about what buyers need in pricing, packaging, audience segments, formats, and integrations, balancing this input with our learner‑first standards and operational quality.

• Establish the operating rhythm for a scaling programmatic business via account planning, outreach cadences, deal hygiene in CRM, pipeline rigor, and repeatable playbooks the next sellers can run.

✅ You have...

• 8+ years in digital advertising, including at least 4 years selling programmatic on the sell side (publisher/platform/app) or in a holding‑company programmatic/investment role, carrying and hitting a quota; demonstrated PMP/PG selling and trading‑desk engagement.

• A demonstrated book of PMP and PG business you personally sourced, negotiated, and grew.

• Experience selling premium mobile or consumer app inventory—especially video and native/custom formats—through programmatic channels to top‑tier advertisers and agencies.

• Strong understanding of ad tech and mobile app ecosystems, including DSP/SSP workflows, deal IDs, verification/measurement, and using data to inform pricing and packaging.

• Excellent communication and presentation skills; clear, concise storytelling for both technical and non‑technical audiences.

⭐ Exceptional candidates will have...

• Deep, current relationships with programmatic leads at major agency holding companies and larger independents.

• Experience moving partners from a heavy open‑auction mix to meaningful always‑on/custom PMP/PG alongside direct sales—and knowing what actually moved the deal (packaging, pricing, supply path, or sales motion).

• Sold against first‑party audience segments or custom data products, not just inventory.

• Hands‑on partnership with Ad Ops on deal setup, SSP onboarding, and campaign QA to improve fill, CPMs, and delivery quality.

We’re hiring a People Relations Business Partner to lead Duolingo’s approach to employee relations, leaves of absence, and workplace accommodations. You will serve as a trusted advisor to Duos, managers, and People Business Partners, bringing sound judgment and consistency to complex employee matters. You’ll manage employee relations cases, own our leave and accommodations programs, and use insights across this work to strengthen our practices and employee experience as Duolingo grows globally.

🧠 You will...

•
Employee Relations

• Manage Employee Relations Cases: Lead employee relations matters from intake through resolution, including employee concerns, workplace conflicts, conduct issues, and other sensitive situations.

• Conduct Investigations: Lead fair, thorough, and timely workplace investigations, documenting findings and partnering with Legal and People Business Partners on appropriate next steps.

• Advise Managers & PBPs: Provide practical guidance on employee concerns, performance and conduct matters, policy interpretation, and complex workplace situations.

• Build ER Practices: Develop tools, guidance, documentation standards, and case management practices that support consistent and thoughtful decision-making.

Leaves & Accommodations

• Own the Programs: Lead Duolingo’s global leave of absence and workplace accommodations programs, including program strategy, employee experience, policies, processes, and continuous improvement.

• Lead Accommodations: Manage workplace accommodation requests from intake through implementation and follow-up, partnering with Duos and managers to identify effective, reasonable solutions.

• Navigate Complex Leaves: Serve as the internal expert and escalation point for complex leave matters, partnering with external administrators, Benefits, Legal, managers, and People Business Partners.

• Support Return to Work: Guide complex return-to-work situations and transitions between leave and workplace accommodations.

• Manage Vendor Performance: Establish clear expectations for external leave and accommodations partners and hold them accountable for service, accuracy, timeliness, and employee experience.

• Support Our Global Workforce: Partner with regional People Business Partners and Legal to navigate leave and accommodation matters across geographies and local requirements.

Insights & Program Improvement

• Surface Trends: Analyze employee relations, leave, and accommodation activity to identify recurring themes, emerging risks, and opportunities for improvement.

• Look Beyond the Case: Connect patterns across individual cases to broader questions about management practices, workload, role design, policies, benefits, accessibility, and the employee experience.

• Turn Insight Into Action: Partner with People leadership, PBPs, Benefits, and Legal to translate what we’re learning into practical improvements.

• Measure Effectiveness: Develop meaningful measures of program health, including timeliness, consistency, outcomes, employee experience, and vendor performance.

People Team Support

• Support PBP Priorities: Provide coordination and project support across select People Business Partner priorities, including documentation, reporting, research, and process work.

• Drive Follow-Through: Help keep defined PBP workstreams organized and moving, bringing strong attention to detail, judgment, and execution.

✅ You have...

• 5+ years of experience across employee relations, workplace accommodations, leave management, HR, or related areas, including experience independently managing complex employee matters.

• Experience conducting workplace investigations and navigating sensitive employee relations matters from intake through resolution.

• Strong working knowledge of workplace accommodations and leave practices, including the ADA, FMLA, and interactive process.

• Experience advising managers and People partners on complex employee situations and translating policies and legal requirements into practical guidance.

• Strong judgment and the ability to navigate sensitive or ambiguous situations with consistency and discretion.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including clear, objective case documentation.

• Strong case management and organizational skills, with careful attention to confidentiality and follow-through.

• Ability to identify patterns across individual cases and translate them into broader organizational insights.

• Comfort working across teams, functions, and geographies in a fast-moving environment.

⭐ Exceptional candidates will have...

• Global Experience: Experience supporting employee relations, leaves, or accommodations across multiple countries or regions.

• Investigations Expertise: Significant experience independently conducting complex workplace investigations.

• Program Building: Experience building or scaling employee relations, leave, or accommodations practices.

• Vendor + System Management: Experience overseeing case management, external leave or accommodations administrators and using performance data to improve service.

• Systems & Insights: Experience using case management systems and employee data to identify trends and inform organizational decisions.

About the role...

The Duolingo English Test (DET) is a high-stakes assessment used by institutions around the world. Its integrity depends on proctors making accurate, consistent, and defensible decisions — even when sessions present ambiguous evidence or new forms of cheating. As the Proctor Quality and Learning Manager (L3) in Scaling Operations, you will own the end-to-end quality standard and learning system that keep our global proctor network aligned and effective as security threats, technology, and workflows evolve. You’ll define what “correct” looks like, run our calibration and adjudication program, and build ongoing training that measurably improves decision quality. You will partner with Psychometrics, Security, Operations, Product, and Engineering to ensure our human and AI-assisted workflows meet rigorous accuracy standards before and after deployment. This is an individual-contributor role within DET Proctoring Operations, with functional leadership over Training Specialists and adjudicators executing the program.

🧠 You will...

• Own the DET proctoring quality standard — maintain rubrics, decision rules, examples, and guidance that define accurate decisions across routine and difficult edge cases.

• Lead calibration and adjudication — operate recurring Proctor Certification Test cycles, resolve disputed decisions, identify patterns of disagreement, and ensure outcomes are consistent and auditable.

• Build and run an ongoing learning program — publish a forward-looking training calendar, deliver monthly interventions, and launch targeted training in response to quality signals, threats, or workflow changes.

• Measure effectiveness — use calibration results, audits, and performance trends to identify learning needs, evaluate training impact, and decide when to clarify standards, retrain, or update guidance.

• Guide specialist execution — set expectations for Training Specialists and adjudicators, assign deliverables, review outputs, and operate onboarding and certification that ramp new specialists quickly.

• Maintain durable sources of truth — keep calibration, adjudication, and training runbooks current so critical processes are documented and auditable.

• Evolve quality alongside proctoring — translate new threats and workflow changes into clear standards, training, and quality controls in partnership with Psychometrics, Security, Operations, Product, and Engineering.

• Represent the proctoring craft — bring frontline proctor evidence into product experiments and workflow decisions; assess whether launched changes preserve decision quality.

• Connect human and technology-assisted quality — establish benchmarks for AI-assisted workflows and validate automated capabilities against real sessions before deployment.

✅ You have...

• 5+ years in assessment development, scoring/rater quality, certification, quality assurance, or a field involving complex, consequential judgments; experience aligning reviewers to a shared standard through calibration programs.

• Adult-learning program experience spanning onboarding, certification, ongoing training, remediation, and effectiveness measurement (beyond one-off materials).

• Exceptional attention to detail and strong judgment in ambiguous cases; ability to produce clear, defensible decisions and guidance.

• Analytical fluency to interpret quality data, disagreement patterns, and performance trends and translate them into practical interventions.

• Clear written and verbal communication; ability to turn complex standards into precise, usable guidance and explain difficult calls.

• Cross-functional leadership without formal authority; experience directing contractors or partners toward clear accountability and outcomes.

• Demonstrated skill in quality standards and rubric design, building living systems with decision logs, change histories, and controls for auditability.

• Experience defining quality benchmarks and validation methods for human–technology workflows, including AI-assisted processes.

• Adaptability — comfort revising standards and programs as risks, products, and technology change.

⭐ Exceptional candidates will have...

• Experience in language assessment, test security, remote proctoring, trust and safety, or fraud prevention in high-integrity environments.

• Experience maintaining quality across large, distributed examiner/rater/reviewer/contractor populations.

• Familiarity with assessment concepts such as inter-rater agreement, reliability, standardization, and performance monitoring.

• Experience designing quality systems that span human judgment and technology-assisted workflows.

• Familiarity with learning-management systems, assessment platforms, quality-audit tools, or operational analytics.

About Watershed

Watershed is the enterprise sustainability platform. Companies like Airbnb, Carlyle Group, FedEx, Visa, and Dr. Martens use Watershed to manage climate and ESG data, produce audit-ready metrics for voluntary and regulatory reporting including CSRD, and drive real decarbonization. We are looking for team members who love product-building, want to work hard at a mission-oriented startup, and will collaborate with us in shaping the culture of a growing team.

We have offices in San Francisco, New York, Denver, London, Paris, Berlin, Sydney, Mexico City, and remote team members across the US and Europe. We hope that you'll be interested in joining us!

The role

Watershed is on a mission to help companies measure, reduce, remove, and report their emissions. We're looking for a strategic operator to join Customer Operations, which runs the programs that deliver on that mission for hundreds of enterprise customers.

You'll partner closely with Customer leadership to design and build the operational backbone for all three teams in our Customer organization: Customer Success, Sustainability Advisory and Services, and Support. That means the engagement models, scalable systems, forecasting infrastructure, and AI-driven workflows the team runs on, plus the reporting leadership uses to steer the business.

This is a role for a hands-on operator who builds what they design and has already rewired their work around AI. You'll operate as a trusted advisor and force multiplier for Customer leadership, owning initiatives end to end from framing the problem to standing up a working solution the team actually uses. You'll help guide the Ops roadmap rather than working a queue, with real scope to define what modern Customer operations looks like at Watershed.

Success means a Customer organization where structural calls like coverage and staffing are made with evidence rather than instinct, customer health scoring actually changes decisions, teams spend their time on customers instead of manual processes, and AI is embedded in how the team operates day to day.

You'll report to the Head of Customer Operations and join a small team of operators who each support a slice of the Customer organization.

This role is based in our New York or San Francisco office, with an expectation of 4 days per week in office.

You will:

• Design and implement the Customer operating model. Partner with Customer leadership across Customer Success, Advisory, and Support on:

• Organizational design, segmentation, and customer engagement models

• Capacity, staffing, and headcount planning

• Target setting and performance frameworks

• Own forecasting from the ground up. Retention, expansion, and services capacity - the methodology, models, and operating cadences that leadership actually trusts, and that surface risk and opportunity early enough to change the outcome

• Build AI-first operational workflows across the customer lifecycle, along with internal tooling that changes how the team operates day to day

• Lead strategic initiatives end to end. Drive complex, multi-workstream Customer org initiatives from conception through implementation. You'll frame problems alongside cross-functional partners, and co-build and co-own the result rather than handing over a recommendation

You might be a fit for this role if:

• You bring 5+ years experience in GTM Operations (CS Ops, RevOps, Strategy & Ops) at a high-growth B2B technology company, or a mix of top-tier strategy consulting and GTM Ops

• You've supported customer-facing teams directly, especially Customer Success. You know how CSMs actually spend their week, you've owned the reporting and operating cadence behind a retention number, and you can tell a real risk or expansion signal from noise

• You have demonstrated analytical excellence. You've built the forecasting models behind real leadership decisions, e.g., capacity, retention, expansion

• You turn ambiguous problems into working systems. You independently take a vague strategic objective through to a plan, a build, and adoption - often as the only person on the problem - and you hold strong opinions about what good looks like

• You're hands-on with GTM and BI tools like Salesforce, Gong, and Sigma. You build your own systems and partner with GTM Engineering on the bigger lifts. Bonus if you're adept with SQL and Salesforce administration, including automation and data model design

• AI is already embedded in how you work. You've shipped AI workflows that other teams actually use, and you have a point of view on how Customer teams should evolve because of it

• You're an exceptional communicator who influences without authority. You can drive alignment across Customer, Product, Data, Sales, and Finance when teams disagree

Must be willing to work from an office 4 days per week (except for remote roles)

Watershed has hub offices in San Francisco, New York, London, and Mexico City and satellite offices in Denver, Sydney, Paris, and Berlin. Where we have offices, employees are expected to be in office for 4 days per week. It starts the same for every candidate: getting to know the team members through 1 to 2 conversations about Watershed, your experience, and your interests. We prioritize transparency and lack of surprise throughout the process.

Who are we?

Cybersecurity helps prevent The Times from becoming news. Our teams work to protect the news makers, their support staff, the platforms they rely on every day, as well as all of The Times' products and services, and our readers who consume them.

• Create an environment that favors context, not control. Empower product engineers and ensure they have the relevant information and tools to deliver secure products and services.

• Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

• Understanding of security controls across a variety of security domains, including access management, encryption, vulnerability management, AI security, network security, authentication/authorization.

• Experience with software engineering practices (CI/CD, GitOps, IaC, etc.) and related security practices (SAST, SCA, secure by design, shift left, etc.).

• A bias towards helping people. Many teams will rely on you to help build their systems.

• Experience with Kubernetes

• Experience with Terraform and Packer

• Experience with HashCorp Vault

The Role

Every Celonis outcome starts with data. As a Solutions Architect, you make sure our customers’ data gets into the Celonis Platform reliably, securely, and at scale, and that insights and actions flow back out into the systems and AI tools where work actually happens.

You’ll join our customer programs team as one of the first technical faces of Celonis. You’ll work hands-on across the full integration toolkit: deploying our out-of-the-box extractors, building custom API connectors in a low-code environment, writing code for push-based ingestion, connecting Celonis to customer lakehouses and LLMs, and configuring writebacks, SSO, and user provisioning. Part implementation consultant, part integration engineer, part trusted technical advisor, this role is ideal for someone early in their career who wants broad exposure to enterprise architecture and modern data and AI integration patterns.

What You’ll Do

Data integration and ingestion

• Implement standard extractors. Install, configure, and troubleshoot Celonis out-of-the-box extractors in customer landscapes, including SAP (ECC and S/4HANA), JDBC-based databases, and cloud applications such as Salesforce, ServiceNow, and others.

• Build custom API connectors. Design and build custom connectors with Celonis Extractor Builder for source systems that expose data through REST or SOAP APIs, handling authentication (OAuth 2.0, API keys, certificates), pagination, rate limits, and incremental (delta) loads.

• Enable push-based ingestion. Help customers design and develop scripts and pipelines (typically in Python) that push data to Celonis via the Data Ingestion API, and advise on file formats, scheduling, and error handling.

• Connect to the lakehouse. Set up zero-copy data sharing between Celonis and customer lakehouses such as Databricks and Microsoft Fabric, including Delta Sharing configuration, access controls, and data freshness.

Actions, AI, and platform connectivity

• Close the loop with writebacks. Configure Action Flows and other integration patterns that write back to customer systems (for example, updating records in SAP, Salesforce, or ticketing tools) so Celonis insights turn into action.

• Connect Celonis to AI. Help customers connect Celonis to their LLMs and AI agents through MCP, covering authentication, permissions, and governance.

Identity, security, and governance

• Own authentication and provisioning. Configure SSO (SAML, OIDC) with identity providers such as Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, and Ping, and set up SCIM-based user and group provisioning.

• Be the security translator. Support customer security, privacy, and compliance reviews, explain the Celonis architecture and data flows, and advise on topics like data minimization, pseudonymization, and least-privilege access.

Customer and team impact

• Scope with confidence. Run technical discovery, document integration architectures and requirements, and estimate effort so projects start on solid footing.

• Be the voice of the field. Escalate product gaps and bugs with clear, reproducible detail, and share field feedback that shapes our integration roadmap.

• Build reusable assets. Contribute reusable connector templates, scripts, runbooks, and best-practice documentation that scale across customers and partners.

What You’ll Bring

• 2–5 years of experience in a technical, customer-facing role such as solutions engineering, integration or implementation consulting, data engineering, or technical consulting.

• Hands-on experience with REST APIs and common authentication patterns (OAuth 2.0, API keys, tokens); comfort using tools like Postman to explore and test APIs.

• Solid programming skills in Python (or a similar language) and strong SQL skills.

• Working knowledge of data pipelines and ETL/ELT concepts, including incremental loads, scheduling, and handling large data volumes.

• Familiarity with identity and access management concepts such as SSO (SAML/OIDC) and SCIM provisioning.

• A basic understanding of networking and security fundamentals (TLS and certificates, proxies, firewalls, VPNs).

• The ability to explain technical topics clearly to both engineers and business stakeholders, and to manage your own workstreams across multiple customer projects.

• Curiosity, ownership, and a bias toward solving problems hands-on.

• A Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Nice to have

• Experience with SAP data structures, tables, or extraction (for example, RFC, ODP, or S/4HANA).

• Experience with at least one major cloud platform (AWS, Azure, GCP) and/or lakehouse platforms such as Databricks, Microsoft Fabric, or Snowflake.

• Exposure to iPaaS or low-code integration tools (for example, MuleSoft, Boomi, Workato, or Power Automate).

• Familiarity with LLMs, AI agents, or MCP.

• Experience with Docker or Linux server administration.

• Relevant certifications (for example, Celonis, cloud, or SAP certifications).

An overview of this role

As Regional Director, Enterprise Sales for the Southeastern United States, you'll lead a team of Strategic Account Executives and own software sales, bookings, and revenue across the region. You'll help new and existing customers adopt GitLab's AI-powered platform for software development, security, and operations (DevSecOps) to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, and reduce security and compliance risk.

Reporting to the AVP, East, you'll hire and develop sales talent, set territory and industry strategies, and align your team's sales plans with GitLab's growth goals. In your first year, you'll focus on building a strong team culture, deepening customer relationships across the Southeast, and meeting or exceeding performance objectives.

GitLab is an open core software company. Our mission is to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world.

This role is fully remote and will be based in the Southeast, US.

What you'll do

• Lead, coach, and develop Strategic Account Executives serving the Southeastern US to deliver software sales, bookings, and revenue results.

• Build and execute territory and industry plans based on market dynamics, customer needs, and competitive trends.

• Establish a sales operating rhythm with clear qualification standards, pipeline hygiene, deal inspection, and accurate forecasts.

• Own sales forecasts, territory management plans, and regional growth strategies aligned with GitLab's revenue goals.

• Track and report on team performance metrics, addressing gaps through coaching and changes to regional plans.

• Partner with Renewals, Marketing, and Sales Operations to manage pipeline health, renewal performance, and deal execution.

• Recruit, hire, and onboard sales talent, and maintain a pipeline of potential future hires in the region.

• Build an inclusive team culture through regular coaching, clear expectations, and ongoing development.

• Enable your team on GitLab's product, pricing, AI-powered DevSecOps positioning, and industry and regulatory factors relevant to US markets.

What you'll bring

• Progressive experience in field sales and sales operations in open source software, DevOps, or a similar software-as-a-service environment. We welcome transferable leadership and regional sales experience from adjacent software markets.

• Success leading and developing account-focused sales teams, including hiring, coaching, and performance management.

• A track record of meeting or exceeding revenue, pipeline, and other sales performance objectives.

• Experience building and executing go-to-market strategies, with a willingness to lead your team and participate directly in selling.

• Commercial and analytical skills to interpret sales performance, market trends, customer needs, and competitive dynamics, and use those insights to improve regional plans.

• Practical experience using customer relationship management (CRM) and sales and marketing tools, such as Salesforce, Clari, or Marketo, to manage forecasts, territories, and pipeline.

• Relationship-building, negotiation, and presentation skills, including executive-level written and verbal communication and the ability to mentor others.

• Interest in open source and a commitment to GitLab's values of collaboration, results, efficiency, diversity, inclusion and belonging, iteration, and transparency.

• Ability to travel as needed and comply with GitLab's travel policy.

About the team

You'll join our Enterprise Sales organization in the US. As an all-remote team, we collaborate across time zones using asynchronous workflows. We drive new and expansion revenue and partner with Renewals, Marketing, and Sales Operations to serve customers across the US.

• Report to an Regional Sales Director and own a broad book of Commercial & Enterprise business, from new prospects to growing existing accounts.

• Manage the full sales cycle for Commercial & Enterprise prospects, from discovery and solution alignment through negotiation and close.

• Support GitLab for Commercial & Enterprise prospects by clearly articulating our DevSecOps value proposition and aligning it to customer business outcomes.

• Analyze wins and losses, contribute to root cause analyses, and share lessons learned with account managers, marketing, and technical teams.

• Document and maintain accurate buying criteria, buying processes, next steps, and owners to ensure a reliable, evidence-based pipeline.

• Contribute to improving our sales handbook and processes by documenting best practices and opportunities for refinement.

• Provide account leadership and direction across pre- and post-sales, partnering closely with technical teams and customer success.

• Represent the voice of the customer by contributing product feedback and ideas to our public issue tracker.

What you’ll bring

• Proven success in software sales, ideally in a Enterprise market context, managing a varied book of business.

• Ability to guide customers through the full buying journey, including defining buying criteria, mapping buying processes, and driving clear next steps.

• Effective communication and interpersonal skills to collaborate with business development, marketing, technical teams, and sales management.

• Experience documenting and maintaining accurate pipeline data and account plans based on evidence rather than assumptions.

• Skill in conducting and contributing to win/loss and root cause analyses, and sharing insights to improve team performance and processes.

• Proficiency in negotiation, presenting to customer stakeholders, and leading commercial discussions to close opportunities.

• Interest in GitLab, open source software, and preferably familiarity with Git, software development tools, or application lifecycle management.

• Alignment with GitLab’s values and an interest in contributing from diverse or transferable sales backgrounds, with willingness to travel in line with company policy.

About the team

The Commercial & Enterprise Sales team focuses on helping growing organizations adopt and expand GitLab’s AI-powered DevSecOps platform across their software delivery lifecycle. You’ll join a distributed group of Account Executives, sales managers, and business development team members who collaborate asynchronously across regions to manage a broad book of business in the mid-market segment. We partner closely with marketing, sales development, and technical teams to run an efficient, transparent sales process, document what works in our sales handbook, and represent the voice of the customer back into GitLab. We focus on opportunities like supporting customers through toolchain consolidation, driving platform adoption, and sharing learnings from wins and losses to continuously improve how we sell and support GitLab.

Your work spans complementary parts of a complete security analysis. On the dependency analysis side, you teach the analysis engine what a project depends on. You parse dependency manifests, lockfiles, and SBOMs so the engine knows which libraries and frameworks are in play and how the code uses them. You also extend the service that turns security advisories into automated merge requests that update vulnerable dependencies. On the vulnerability detection side, you grow GitLab's security analysis engine with hybrid analyzers that blend rule-based detection and AI reasoning. You build and apply the tooling that develops, evaluates, and ships those analyzers, and you measure how well they find real problems. That work also expands coverage of the libraries, frameworks, and AI agent tooling that real-world applications are built on.

These threads reinforce each other. What a project depends on, and how its code uses those dependencies, are parts of one picture, and this team works across all of it. We make thoughtful use of AI-assisted development tools in our daily work. We expect you to use them effectively and with good judgment.

What you do

• Act as the directly responsible individual (DRI) for team initiatives from design through delivery, shipping with minimal guidance in partnership with the technical lead

• Bring systems built by one engineer to team ownership through documentation, tests, and shared review

• Design and ship analyzers that pair deterministic analysis capabilities with AI-driven analysis, and build the evaluation harnesses that measure their false positives and missed findings against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, raising the bar for what counts as a trustworthy result. That includes detection rules mapped to CWE and the test fixtures that prove they work.

• Package those analyzers for every place GitLab runs them, including CI jobs, AI agent workflows, and command-line tools, with findings reported in GitLab's standard security report formats

• Design and ship the manifest, lockfile, and SBOM parsing that tells the static analysis engine what a project depends on, and extend it to new ecosystems and formats

• Ship features across the automated remediation service that turns security advisories into dependency update merge requests, from sandboxed updates to merge request creation

• Solve technical problems of high scope and complexity, actively seek out difficult impediments affecting the whole team, and advocate for improvements to quality, security, and performance with Product Management, Engineering stakeholders such as Frontend and UX, and partner teams such as Code Scanning and Composition Analysis

• Mentor Intermediate engineers through code review and pairing, and maintain our internal standards for style, maintainability, and best practices through review

• Participate in on-call rotations to assist troubleshooting product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues

What you bring

• Experience building your own LLM tooling, such as a harness, an agent pipeline, or evaluations, with the judgment to know when output is trustworthy and when it isn't

• Substantial professional experience writing and testing production code in a systems language, particularly Go and/or Rust, with depth in at least one. We use both, plus Ruby on the remediation side and Python for some analyzers, and value willingness to work across them.

• Familiarity with package managers and dependency management in one or more language ecosystems, such as npm, Maven, pip, Bundler, or Cargo. Experience building tooling around them is better still.

• Demonstrated application security experience, such as vulnerability research, secure code review, or writing detection rules, and fluency with vulnerability classes (OWASP Top 10, CWE) and the software supply chain

• A track record of taking ownership of ambiguous problems and shipping with minimal guidance, with the self-motivation and organizational skills suited to a remote, largely asynchronous environment

• Demonstrated capacity to communicate clearly and concisely about technical problems, and to write design proposals that bring a team to a decision

Helpful experience

• Experience evaluating AI-driven detection against labeled data, including measuring false positives and missed findings

• Experience with performance optimization at scale

• Hands-on program analysis experience, such as parsing, ASTs, or data-flow analysis

• Familiarity with popular web or mobile application frameworks and how they handle input, data, and configuration

• Experience with containerized workflows and CI/CD (we use Docker heavily)

About the team

The Security Factory: Code Security team builds GitLab's code-level security scanning capabilities, spanning static application security testing and dependency scanning. We help developers find and fix security issues in both the code they write and the open source components they depend on, as early as possible.

We work closely with the Static Analysis team on GitLab's SAST engines, with Composition Analysis on the broader software supply chain, and with other groups across the Sec Section. We rely heavily on asynchronous work across time zones.

Remote-Global

• A solution to capture the state of a customer’s server for easier troubleshooting

• A functionality to ChatOps to make it easier to identify user accounts on GitLab.com

• Contribute to building and refining internal support tools and workflows, including automation and troubleshooting utilities, to make diagnosing and resolving issues more efficient.

• Support the growth of the team by reviewing applications and assessments, and participating in interviews and hiring decision discussions.

• Strong Linux systems administration knowledge, with the ability to troubleshoot performance and configuration issues in complex environments

This is the most senior IC role on the team: you'll own architecture for our most consequential, cross-org infrastructure initiatives, and be the person other senior and staff engineers look to when a design decision needs to hold up across every team that depends on it. Recent and current flagship work at this level includes leading the Istio service mesh rollout as single-threaded owner across the entire organization; shaping the architecture behind our Multi-Region Resilience Program; and owning the technical direction of our AI-enriched Service Catalog. You'll operate at the intersection of deep technical execution and org-wide influence, staying hands-on in critical code and infrastructure paths while setting the patterns other teams build on.

You Will:

• Own group-critical platform initiatives: Take single-threaded ownership of multi-quarter, cross-org programs — service mesh adoption across independent clusters and business units, multi-region resilience strategy, and foundational platform initiatives. Align systems and abstractions to long-term organizational strategy.

• Set direction others build on: Define the architectural patterns, golden paths, and platform primitives (Istio mTLS/traffic policy, AI agent golden paths, MCP-backed service APIs) that other engineers implement against. Create shared components that improve delivery consistency across teams rather than one-off solutions per squad.

• Lead through hands-on technical excellence: Stay deeply engaged in the hardest parts of the systems you own — debugging production incidents at the mesh layer, hardening migration tooling, resolving cross-team architectural conflicts — earning credibility through visible, high-quality technical work rather than through title alone.

• Drive execution across organizational boundaries: Coordinate rollouts that depend on multiple engineering orgs contributing resources on a schedule (e.g., a named engineering champion per business unit for a service mesh migration). Anticipate systemic blockers — resourcing gaps, conflicting migration sequencing, environment drift between staging and production — and resolve them before they stall the program.

• Own testing infrastructure strategy end-to-end: Serve as DRI for how engineering teams validate changes before production, spanning iteration environments, pre-prod confidence gates, and multi-service validation for cross-service changes.

• Mentor Staff and Senior engineers: Coach engineers below you on system design, migration strategy, and how to navigate ambiguity in cross-team initiatives. Raise the technical bar of the org by example, not just by review.

• Drive org-wide reduction of technical debt and cost: Lead large-scale infrastructure consolidations and migrations (CI/CD platform changes, artifact registry modernization, dependency upgrades) end-to-end, with the rollout discipline, cost modeling, and stakeholder communication that a multi-hundred-repo change demands.

• Establish the metrics that prove platform investment works: Define and drive adoption of the leading indicators — adoption rate, incident trends, cost trajectory, developer sentiment — that let leadership see platform work as a business asset, not overhead.

You Have:

• 12+ years in Platform, Infrastructure, DevOps, or SRE roles, including demonstrated ownership of at least one initiative that spanned multiple teams or business units, not just a single team's roadmap.

• Deep, production-proven expertise in Kubernetes/EKS, service mesh (Istio strongly preferred — mTLS, traffic shaping, sidecar architecture, multi-cluster rollout), and Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform or similar) at meaningful scale.

• A track record of leading complex, multi-quarter technical programs from architecture through execution — including the ability to produce the kind of cost/risk analysis and phased proposal that secures leadership buy-in and funding.

• Experience debugging and resolving production incidents in distributed, multi-hop systems (e.g., proxy/sidecar-layer failures, cross-service auth issues, environment-specific config drift between staging and production).

• Proficiency in at least one of Go, Python, TypeScript, or Java, with the judgment to know when to write code yourself versus when to set direction and delegate.

• A demonstrated ability to influence without direct authority — driving alignment across engineering orgs that don't report to you, and building the kind of technical credibility that makes other senior engineers want to build on your patterns rather than route around them.

• Experience mentoring Staff-level engineers and shaping how a broader engineering org approaches system design, not just your immediate team.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Experience with AI-native platform tooling: agentic tooling, MCP-backed APIs and golden paths for deploying AI agents in production.

• A track record of driving large-scale cost or infrastructure consolidation initiatives (CI/CD platform migrations, cloud cost optimization, vendor consolidation) with measurable business impact.

H&H is seeking a Manager, Environmental Compliance & Sustainability to manage a team of Environmental Specialists and administer environmental compliance programs for U.S. and Canadian operations, with support for locations in the European Union, Australia, and Japan and for the company's greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) projects. • Serve as a subject matter expert (SME) in environmental compliance and sustainability, advising Operations (including fulfillment), Engineering, Pharmacy and Lab teams, Legal, Packaging, and site leadership.

• Manage, coach, and develop Environmental Specialists: assign work, set priorities, and review deliverables. Serve as their escalation point for complex regulatory, permitting, and waste questions.

• Administer corporate environmental programs and standards established by senior environmental and workplace health & safety leadership (hazardous waste, Tier II and other recurring reporting, KPIs) and ensure consistent application across U.S. and Canadian sites.

• Review site-level compliance programs, permits, and regulatory submissions prepared by specialists (hazardous waste, HMBP, air, wastewater, stormwater, SPCC) for alignment with CAA, CWA, RCRA, EPCRA, and company standards.

• Execute the environmental monitoring/peer review program across locations, review findings, and verify that corrective actions are completed and closed.

• Support site leadership on significant inspections and enforcement matters by preparing technical information and responses; serve as the Operations liaison for routine inspections.

• Review waste characterization and profiling for new Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) and other waste streams, and guide sites on compliant handling and disposal at pharmacy, lab, and fulfillment operations.

• Manage day-to-day performance of waste management vendors and environmental service providers within scope and agreements established by senior leadership.

• Support waste reduction, diversion, recycling, and circular economy initiatives with Supply Chain and Operations; identify and recommend sustainability opportunities across assigned locations and implement approved programs.

• Support the GHG emissions inventory and EPR projects, including data and packaging information gathering, registrations, and reporting, in coordination with internal data owners and external consultants.

• When necessary, provide compliance and program support to locations in the European Union, Australia, and Japan, working with local teams and advisors within the company's established framework.

• Provide environmental review for new builds, retrofits, and acquisitions, partnering with Project Management and Engineering.

• Maintain and update environmental policies, procedures, and training content for approval by senior leadership.

You Have

• Bachelor's degree in environmental science or management, engineering, industrial technology, business, or a related field.

• 8+ years of experience in environmental compliance, with demonstrated subject matter expertise in hazardous waste and environmental regulatory programs and working knowledge of sustainability and waste reduction practices.

• Experience managing or leading environmental, health, and safety (EHS) employees or other technical staff, including reviewing regulatory submissions and providing technical guidance.

• Working knowledge of federal, state, and provincial environmental regulations (CAA, CWA, RCRA, EPCRA) and strong multi-site hazardous waste program experience, including permitting, reporting (e.g., Tier II), agency inspections, and audits.

• Experience managing waste vendors and supporting waste reduction and recycling programs.

• Ability to support GHG accounting and packaging EPR projects, working with internal teams and external consultants.

• Strong project management, analytical, and communication skills, and the ability to work in a matrixed environment.

• Experience with environmental data management and reporting tools.

• Willingness to travel up to 30% of the time, including regular travel to company sites in North America and potential international travel.

Preferred Qualifications

• Master’s degree in environmental management, environmental science, or a related field.

• Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM) certification (strongly preferred).

• Familiarity with packaging EPR requirements, recycling schemes, and circular economy principles.

About the Role:

The best SDETs in the industry are no longer measured by how many tests they write. They're measured by the systems they build that decide whether software is safe to ship — and, increasingly, by how well they wield AI to do it.

That's the role we're hiring for. We're looking for a Senior Staff SDET to own quality architecture and engineering strategy for our most critical systems, and to lead how we apply AI across our entire testing and release pipeline. You'll build the frameworks, platforms, and agent-driven workflows that the rest of engineering depends on, define what "safe to ship" means here, and stay deep in the code while doing it.

This is a genuinely hands-on senior technical leadership role with impact that spans many teams. If you want to build AI-native quality systems rather than bolt AI tools onto a legacy suite, this is that job.

Why This Role Is Different

• AI is the core of the work. You'll own how we use LLMs and agents for test generation, failure triage, self-healing, and release decisioning — and you'll set the guardrails that keep it trustworthy.

• You'll test AI, not just test with it. We ship AI-powered product features, which means building evaluation harnesses, golden datasets, and probabilistic assertions for systems that don't return the same answer twice. This is frontier work with very little established playbook.

• Real autonomy and real scope. You'll set the technical direction for quality engineering, not inherit someone else's strategy.

You Will:

Own quality architecture and strategy

• Own quality architecture for our most critical systems and initiatives, defining long-term quality strategy aligned with business and product goals.

• Design shared quality platforms, automation frameworks, and test infrastructure that are adopted across multiple teams.

• Establish quality patterns and guardrails that scale across teams, eliminating duplicated, brittle, or low-signal testing approaches through platform-level solutions.

• Anticipate systemic quality and reliability risks and drive preventative architectural solutions before they impact customers.

• Set the standard for what "great" looks like in quality engineering at scale.

Lead our AI-driven testing strategy

• Define and drive our strategy for AI-assisted testing — autonomous test generation, intelligent test selection, agent-based failure triage, and self-healing automation — with a clear-eyed view of where each genuinely pays off and where it adds noise.

• Build the guardrails that make AI-driven testing trustworthy: knowing when a self-healing agent is masking a real regression versus absorbing harmless implementation drift is the difference between leverage and liability.

• Orchestrate AI agents as part of the CI/CD decision pipeline, turning raw test signal into release confidence rather than more dashboards.

• Own quality for our AI-powered product features — designing eval suites, golden datasets, LLM-as-judge scorers, and statistical approaches for non-deterministic behavior, plus testing for hallucination, safety, and response stability.

• Establish how we test AI-generated application code, validating behavioral correctness and not just syntactic plausibility.

• Evaluate emerging AI testing tooling with real rigor, and be honest about what doesn't work.

Raise the bar operationally and across the team

• Lead the operational maturity of our quality systems and signals — defining quality metrics, dashboards, and release confidence indicators, and leading post-incident analysis that informs architectural and process improvements.

• Produce exemplary technical artifacts — quality architecture documents, automation frameworks, test platforms — that set the bar for the rest of the team, while staying hands-on in critical quality systems and automation code paths.

• Serve as the accountable technical leader for strategic initiatives, proactively managing reliability, scalability, and technical debt across teams.

• Mentor senior SDETs, quality engineers, and other senior technical leaders — especially on building AI fluency into their practice.

• Establish hiring standards, coaching, and talent development.

• Champion customer-centric quality decisions, ensuring technical trade-offs reflect real user needs and long-term product value.

• Partner with Engineering and Product leadership to embed scalability and resilience into roadmap planning, not just technical design.

You Have:

• 10+ years of hands-on experience in quality engineering or SDET roles, including experience architecting quality strategy and automation platforms across multiple teams.

• Proven track record designing and scaling test automation frameworks across the full stack — frontend web, mobile, and backend/API (e.g., Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, Appium, Postman, or similar).

• Deep proficiency in one or more programming languages (e.g., JavaScript, TypeScript, Kotlin) used to build and maintain shared automation frameworks and tooling. You write production-quality code, not just test scripts.

• Hands-on experience applying AI to testing — LLM-assisted test generation, agent-based workflows, intelligent test selection, or self-healing automation — with informed opinions about where it delivers and where it disappoints.

• Demonstrated ability to define quality architecture and standards that scale across many teams, including shared quality platforms and test infrastructure.

• Strong grasp of modern development and delivery practices (agile/lean, DevOps, shift-left testing, TDD) and experience embedding quality gates into CI/CD systems (e.g., GitHub Actions, CircleCI, Jenkins).

• Experience mentoring and developing senior quality engineers and senior technical leaders, with a track record of raising the technical bar across a group or organization.

• History of leading post-incident and root-cause analysis that drives architectural and process change.

• Excellent judgment on trade-offs between short-term delivery and long-term system resilience and maintainability.

• Strong executive communication skills, with the ability to influence engineering and product leadership on quality strategy, risk, and investment.

• Experience with performance and load testing at scale.

Nice to Have:

• Familiarity with LLM observability and evaluation tooling (e.g., Braintrust, Arize, MLflow, LangSmith, or similar).

About the Role:

We are seeking a highly motivated, detail-oriented Manager, Production Planning to lead the planning team responsible for our non-sterile compounded production. This position manages and develops the site's production planners and owns the forward-looking production plan. The plan converts demand forecasts and inventory policy into a rolling view of the next several weeks through the next year or more, tests that plan against labor, equipment, and material capacity, and identifies where the business cannot meet it. The Manager then drives the response to each gap, whether through training, labor, or capital investment, and hands the plan to Production Scheduling for on-site execution. The ideal candidate is a proactive people leader with a strong understanding of integrated planning systems, supply chain dynamics, and cross-functional collaboration across the operations planning team.

You Will:

• Lead, manage, and develop the team of production planners, setting priorities, coaching, reviewing output, and ensuring consistent planning practices and coverage.

• Own the development and maintenance of mid- and long-term production plans for non-sterile compounded products in alignment with demand forecasts and inventory policies.

• Define the planning horizons, plan-of-record cadence, and frozen window, and publish the plan to Production Scheduling on a fixed schedule.

• Manage finished goods inventory for compounded products within company guidance while maintaining click-to-deliver metrics for customers.

• Develop what-if scenarios that identify where and when the plan exceeds available capacity, and which constraints are most sensitive to demand, product mix, batch size, and shift patterns.

• Articulate and document all risks resulting from production capacity constraints, including volume at risk, timing, and effect on delivery and inventory. If the plan cannot be met, make or recommend revisions when plans cannot be met, and document the reason for each revision.

• Recommend and size actions to close each gap, including training and cross-training for skill coverage, hiring and labor planning, overtime and shift design, equipment and facility investment, and outsourcing. Partner with Compounding Operations, HR, and Quality to carry out approved actions and track whether each one delivers the capacity it was sized to deliver.

• Monitor plan attainment, forecast accuracy, and capacity utilization at the weekly and monthly level, analyze variances, and implement corrective actions.

• Use actual cycle times, yields, and throughput reported by Production Scheduling to update planning standards and capacity model assumptions.

• Collaborate cross-functionally across the operations planning team, partnering with demand planning to communicate forecast discrepancies and agree on the plan of record, with production scheduling to confirm the plan can be executed and take in the constraints it escalates, and with procurement and raw materials planning to confirm material availability.

• Develop and maintain tools, dashboards, and KPIs that communicate plan status, constraints, risks, and performance to plan to leadership.

You Have:

• 8+ years experience in at least 1 of the following: Production planning, capacity planning, or resource planning, with demonstrated experience leading or developing others.

• Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Operations, Industrial Engineering, or related field required; APICS/CPIM certification a plus.

• Experience building capacity models and presenting investment, staffing, or outsourcing recommendations to senior leaders.

• Proficient in inventory management concepts with an understanding of the financial and operational implications of planning decisions.

• Experience in pharmaceutical or pharmacy production/manufacturing environments is a plus.

• Excel proficiency including experience with data manipulations – Lookups, PivotTables, External Data Connections.

• Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities and lead a team in a fast-paced environment.
